name: Capacit'e Infraprojects Ltd
tagline: Cheap-vs-peers EPC contractor with a 5x-revenue order book and a de-pledging promoter, working through a temporary commodity-cost margin squeeze and a fresh receivables flag
business_overview: Capacit'e Infraprojects is an EPC (engineering, procurement, construction) contractor specializing in turnkey solutions for housing, high-rises, super high-rises, specialty buildings, and urban infrastructure.
fundamentals_table: ~9.0x (screener.in, Sep 2026) vs. mid-cap civil construction peers at 15-22x
Rs 2,623-2,644 Cr (+12% YoY) / Rs 193 Cr (sources vary slightly on exact revenue)
Rs 13,535 Cr as of Jun 30, 2026 (~5.1x TTM revenue); FY27 order-inflow guidance Rs 4,500-5,000 Cr
Revenue Rs 629 Cr (+7% YoY), EBITDA margin 15.7% (down from 17.2%), PAT Rs 39.4 Cr (down from Rs 45.7 Cr) on a Rs 10 Cr commodity provision
151 days (vs historical 100-120 range); working capital days ~128
18.65% of promoter holding (Jun-2026), down from ~31.9%; management targeting zero by FY27-end
fundamentals_narrative: Trades meaningfully cheaper than mid-cap civil construction peers (~9.0x P/E vs. 15-22x, and below book value at 0.86x P/B) despite consistent double-digit revenue growth and a very large order book relative to revenue (~5.1x TTM). Q1 FY27 PAT declined YoY on a Rs 10 Cr commodity provision, which management guides to partially reverse in Q3/Q4 FY27 as government escalation-index reimbursement catches up to spot input costs. Revenue growth itself decelerated (FY26 +12% YoY annual -> Q1 FY27 +7% YoY) on early-quarter labour shortages. Two new, previously-uncaptured facts this pass cut in opposite directions: promoters cut their pledge from ~32% to 18.65% of holding in a single quarter (genuine de-risking, targeting zero by FY27-end), while the FY26 statutory auditor issued a qualified opinion flagging ~Rs 66 Cr of receivables (Rs 11.56 Cr from a CIRP-insolvent party plus ~Rs 54.9 Cr under legal proceedings) as uncertain to recover -- consistent with, and now quantifying, the working-capital risk this file already flagged.
sentiment_summary: Read most recent 50 of 165 posts (single batch, no escalation). Two substantive recent posts (Jun and Aug 2026) both frame the story positively -- a value re-rating candidate with a temporary, explainable margin headwind.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users posted in this thread. austin (Jun 2026) called Q4 numbers decent across line items with consistent growth guidance, noting the stock trades cheap vs. peers and inflationary cost increases are being passed through per contract terms, with margin impact not yet meaningfully visible. Aiyappaa (Aug 2026, 4 loves) posted a detailed Q4 FY26/Q1 FY27 concall summary: confirmed the valuation gap vs. peers, and explained the Q1 FY27 PAT dip as a Rs 20 Cr commodity provisioning charge (accounting prudence) driven by a sharp Feb-May spike in non-ferrous input costs (aluminum +35-40%, copper, electricals), where government WPI/CPWD escalation-index reimbursement lags spot prices by 1-2 quarters -- i.e., a timing mismatch expected to normalize, not a structural margin loss. Note: this pass's own concall-transcript research found the company's own stated figure to be a Rs 10 Cr additional provision, not Rs 20 Cr -- discrepancy unresolved, see deep_dive.open_questions.
bse_notes: 6-month BSE/NSE scan (this pass): Apr-2026 Rs 295 Cr LoA from Indus Co-operative Housing Society (Wadala, Mumbai residential+commercial) added to order book. Apr-2026 disclosure that promoters/PAC created no fresh encumbrance during FY25-26. May-2026 and Jun-2026 promoter pledge releases (10L then 25.5L shares), cutting pledge to 18.65% of promoter holding. FY26 results (AGM 24-Jul-2026) carried the auditor's qualified opinion on ~Rs 66 Cr of receivables. No rating action, M&A, buyback, dividend, or KMP/auditor-change news found in the window.
bull_case: Trades at a real, quantified discount to peers (~9.0x P/E vs. 15-22x peer range, below book value) despite consistent growth

Order book of Rs 13,535 Cr is ~5.1x TTM revenue -- strong multi-year revenue visibility, reinforced by continued order inflow (Rs 295 Cr LoA Apr-2026) and a reiterated FY27 order-inflow guidance of Rs 4,500-5,000 Cr

Q1 FY27 margin/PAT dip has a specific, well-documented, timing-based explanation (commodity cost spike vs. lagged government escalation-clause reimbursement) rather than a demand or competitive problem, corroborated by both a detailed community concall summary and this pass's own concall-transcript research

Promoters cut pledge from ~32% to 18.65% of holding in a single quarter (35.5 lakh shares released, May-Jun 2026) and are targeting zero pledge by FY27-end -- genuine de-risking, not the pattern of a promoter preparing to exit (promoter holding itself has stayed flat at 31.69% for four straight quarters)
bear_case: Revenue growth itself is modest and decelerating (Q1 FY27 revenue +7% YoY vs. FY26's +12% YoY) -- this is more a re-rating/value case than a high-growth story

EPC businesses carry structural working-capital and execution risk: debtor days are elevated at 151 (vs. a historical 100-120 range), and the FY26 statutory auditor issued a qualified opinion flagging ~Rs 66 Cr of receivables (Rs 11.56 Cr from a party under CIRP/insolvency, ~Rs 54.9 Cr under legal proceedings) as uncertain to recover -- a new, quantified asset-quality flag this pass

The 'temporary, will normalize' framing for the commodity provisioning rests on government escalation-clause reimbursement catching up, which is outside the company's direct control; the provision's own size is disputed between sources (company concall: Rs 10 Cr; community VP-thread estimate: Rs 20 Cr), unresolved this pass
No dividend despite consistent profitability, and ROE remains subdued (~10.4%) -- shareholder-returns discipline is a soft but real negative
verdict_headline: Cheap value-plus-order-book story with a well-explained (though not fully consensus-verified) margin dip and a genuinely de-risking promoter -- offset this pass by a fresh auditor receivables flag and a growth deceleration
verdict_reasoning: The combination of a large order book (5.1x revenue), a genuine valuation discount to peers, a well-documented timing-based explanation for the recent margin dip, and now a promoter actively cutting pledge supports the thesis, particularly if the peer-multiple gap closes

But underlying revenue growth is modest and decelerated further in Q1 FY27 (+7% YoY vs. FY26's +12%), and this pass surfaced a new, quantified auditor qualification on ~Rs 66 Cr of receivables -- so the 10x case here depends more on multiple re-rating and order-book conversion than on outsized organic growth, and carries more near-term asset-quality noise than the prior pass captured

Four-box score stays at 2.5 (tailwind weak, tam yes, moat no, valuation yes) -- the written exception (valuation box = yes) keeps thesis_fit at 10x-in-2-3-years per the decision table, with conviction capped Low-Medium and an 'unconfirmed' caveat given EPC's inherent working-capital/execution risk and market_expectation.evidence_quality now reading weak (thesis-critical commitments are still guidance-stage, not yet delivered)

four_box.note: Modest, decelerating revenue growth (+7% Q1 FY27 vs +12% FY26) suggests this is a valuation catch-up story more than a structural growth tailwind (weak); order book (~5.1x TTM revenue) plus reiterated FY27 order-inflow guidance (Rs4,500-5,000cr) gives strong multi-year tam visibility (yes); no explicit moat for a mid-cap EPC business (no); trades at ~9.0x P/E vs 15-22x peers and below book (0.86x P/B) -- a real, quantified valuation discount (yes). Written exception (valuation=yes) keeps thesis_fit at 10x-in-2-3-years despite score < 3.0, conviction capped Low-Medium.
